desc: Sort arrays A, B, C in descending order.
Implement a Max-Heap (using negative values in Python's `heapq`) to store tuples of `(value, i, j, k)`.
Initialize the heap with the triplet $(0, 0, 0)$ (0-indexed) corresponding to the largest value.
Maintain a `visited` set to store visited triplets $(i, j, k)$ to avoid processing duplicates.
Pop the largest element from the heap.
If this is the K-th iteration, record the value and break.
Generate neighbors by incrementing one index at a time: $(i+1, j, k)$, $(i, j+1, k)$, $(i, j, k+1)$.
For each neighbor, if indices are within bounds $[0, N-1]$ and not in `visited`, add to heap and `visited`.
Print the recorded K-th largest value.
Write the complete Python script to stdin/stdout.
Run the code against Sample 1 to verify output is 31.
